usage: xo build [--targets=all|os/arch,...] [--backend=go|llvm|arm64|amd64|wasm] [--no-gc]
                [--no-mono] [--no-arenas] [--tzdata=embedded|system] [--ci]
                [--release] [--debug-contracts=on|off] [--dbg=on|off]
                [--error-args=on|off] [--debug-info=on|off|split]
                [--profile-support=on|off] [--trace-support=on|off] [--opt=O0..O3]
                [-s] [--dsym] [--ld=macho|cc] [--race]
                [--stamp NAME=VALUE]... [--hybrid]
                [--json] [-o out] <dirs...>

Compile to static binaries (default: the host). The directories are one
program. The default backend is native (decisions 0248 and 0270): arm64
or amd64 for the target's architecture, --race too where a
ThreadSanitizer runtime ships for the target (else llvm, which needs
clang). With no --backend, --targets=all builds each of linux/amd64,
linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64 and wasip1/wasm
with its own native backend, as NAME-OS-ARCH (.exe, .wasm) in -o's
directory; windows/arm64 needs --backend=go, whose --targets=all builds
all seven; -o NAME for windows writes NAME.exe. --backend=go builds through
the Go toolchain, and a program with `use go` needs it. A linux/arm64
target links with Xo's own linker, from any host (decision 0243).
--no-gc (also on run and test) reports every construct, std API, or
effect the native backends do not support as XO1201 before code
generation (decision 0083). --backend=wasm builds a WASI preview1 module.
Request scoped arenas for HTTP handlers are on by default (decision
0066); --no-arenas (also on run and test) turns them off. --ci fails
before building when a .xo file is not formatted (core 10.5) or dbg(...)
is left in code (core 11.4). --release is a preset (decision 0354):
it turns off --debug-contracts (requires(debug) and ensures(debug)
compiled out), --dbg (dbg(x) is x), --debug-info, --profile-support (the
runtime's XO_PROF) and --trace-support (XO_TRACE's recorder), and sets
--opt=O2; each setting can be given either way in any build, and an
explicit flag wins over the preset (a bare flag means on; on|off and
true|false both work). --error-args=off drops parameter values from
error frames. --opt applies to the LLVM backend (a usage error on arm64
and amd64; the Go backend ignores it). --debug-info=split is not
implemented yet (decision 0355). Native builds carry DWARF line tables
(in a darwin binary's __DWARF segment, a link through cc's too; --dsym
also writes NAME.dSYM); -s leaves them and the local symbols out.
--ld picks the native
linker: macho (Xo's own; the default on darwin/arm64) or cc. --race (also
on run and test) builds with ThreadSanitizer on the LLVM backend. --stamp (repeatable, also on run)
sets a `const NAME: Str` of the main module for this build (XO1501
otherwise). std/time zone data is embedded per use (decision 0094);
--tzdata=system (also on run and test) reads the host's database
instead. --hybrid is deprecated: a plain Go backend build with a
warning (decision 0084).

A directory means that directory alone; DIR/... covers the directories
below it too, up to 6,000 .xo files or 60,000 entries (decision 0345).
A DIR/... with no .xo file at or below DIR is an error.
